scope: Individual assault occupied-destination intent versus CBE partner alternate-entry nodes

source.range: same-floor position selection and stopped-unit occupied target adjustment

intent: Avoid an occupied destination obstructing an individual assault approach.
disposition: Implement bounded preference among physically visited native points; do not copy random displacement or infer accessible floor from arbitrary surface hits.
cbe: Shared occupancy now includes physical positions of up to eight current eligible pair workers even without an issued movement receipt, plus current owned approach targets.
Partner fallback ranks free eligible same-floor visited points ahead of occupied points and rechecks free-space preference inside its existing command/attempt transaction.
All-occupied cases retain existing finite fallback; no hard reservation, deadline extension, new ray/world query, teleport or visit credit.
limitations: Proximity is an admission preference, not a path-clearance or room-safety proof.
Live participants only; nonparticipant occupancy and native path choice remain engine constraints.
Two-and-a-half metre/floor-band preference can be conservative across thin walls; all-occupied fallback remains finite.
Entry coherence, repeatability, hostile rooms, casualty/HC behavior and runtime cost remain physically unverified.
